title: The Man Who Stole A Plane For A Bar Bet
sources: New York Times (October 1, 1956): Stolen Plane Lands on St. Nicholas Ave
New York Times (October 5, 1958): Second Stolen Flight by Thomas Fitzpatrick
National Air and Space Museum: The Fitzpatrick Flights

lines.text: A pilot just crash-landed a stolen plane on a Manhattan street.
lines.caps: PILOT CRASH-LANDED | A STOLEN PLANE | ON MANHATTAN STREET

lines.text: And he only did it to win a drunken ten-dollar bet.
lines.caps: HE ONLY DID IT | TO WIN A DRUNKEN | TEN-DOLLAR BET

lines.text: In nineteen fifty-six, Tommy was drinking at a New York bar.
lines.caps: IN NINETEEN FIFTY-SIX | TOMMY WAS DRINKING | AT NEW YORK BAR

lines.text: A patron claimed nobody could fly from New Jersey in fifteen minutes.
lines.caps: PATRON CLAIMED NOBODY | COULD FLY FROM JERSEY | IN FIFTEEN MINUTES

lines.text: Tommy snuck into a flight field and hijacked a single-engine plane.
lines.caps: TOMMY SNUCK IN | HIJACKED A PLANE | WITH ZERO LIGHTS

lines.text: He flew completely in the pitch-dark without radio or lights.
lines.caps: HE FLEW COMPLETELY | IN PITCH-DARK | WITHOUT RADIO OR LIGHTS

lines.text: Then, he touched down smoothly right outside the tavern door.
lines.caps: TOUCHED DOWN SMOOTHLY | RIGHT OUTSIDE | THE TAVERN DOOR

lines.text: The stunned plane owner was so impressed he dropped all charges.
lines.caps: STUNNED PLANE OWNER | WAS SO IMPRESSED | DROPPED ALL CHARGES

lines.text: The judge only gave Tommy a small hundred-dollar fine.
lines.caps: THE JUDGE ONLY GAVE | A SMALL HUNDRED-DOLLAR | CASH FINE

lines.text: Two years later, another patron refused to believe the story.
lines.caps: TWO YEARS LATER | ANOTHER PATRON | REFUSED TO BELIEVE

lines.text: So Tommy stole another plane and landed on the exact same street.
lines.caps: SO HE STOLE ANOTHER | AND LANDED ON | THE EXACT SAME STREET

lines.text: Proving to every skeptic in New York why...
lines.caps: PROVING TO EVERY | SKEPTIC IN NEW YORK | EXACTLY WHY
